summary: Exfiltrates OxaPay payment API keys and opens a remote-controlled TCP proxy backdoor to a hardcoded bare-IP controller
details: On invocation of crb()/startControlClient(), the package reads OXAPAY_GENERAL_API_KEY, OXAPAY_MERCHANT_API_KEY, OXAPAY_PAYOUT_API_KEY, and OXAPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET from process.env, together with the host's non-loopback IPv4 address and NEXTAUTH_URL/VERCEL_URL-derived domain, and POSTs them to a hardcoded bare-IP plain-HTTP endpoint at http://23.160.168.168:4141/register. It additionally enumerates a fixed set of Next.js/Vercel hosting env vars (DOMAIN, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, VERCEL_URL, NEXTAUTH_URL, AUTH_URL, APP_URL, etc.) to include in the register payload. The client then opens a WebSocket to ws://23.160.168.168:4141/proxy-tunnel and, on receiving messages of shape {type:'open', host, port}, calls net.createConnection to attacker-chosen host:port and pipes base64-encoded bytes bidirectionally between that socket and the remote controller — a full arbitrary-outbound TCP proxy under remote control, usable to pivot into internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, and other hosts reachable from the installer. The destination is a bare IPv4 over plain HTTP/WS with no TLS, no publisher domain, and no relationship to the package name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
